operations.before: [F2] A $C^1$ diffeomorphism changes a density by dividing by the absolute derivative of the inverse map. [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
operations.after: [F2] A $C^1$ diffeomorphism changes a density by multiplying by the absolute derivative of the inverse map. [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]

defect: The reciprocal has already been taken in D(h^{-1}); multiplying by its absolute value is the density rule. Dividing by that inverse derivative would give the opposite Jacobian factor.
actual_correct_proof_witness: 3.1 For $t>0$, $W_t$ has density $\phi_t$ by [F5], and the change-of-variables formula [F2] gives $\displaystyle p_t(x)=\frac{\phi_t(h^{-1}(x))}{h'(h^{-1}(x))}.$ Likewise, for $0\le s<t$ its transition density is $\displaystyle q(s,x;t,y)=\frac{\phi_{t-s}(h^{-1}(y)-h^{-1}(x))}{h'(h^{-1}(y))}.$ These densities are positive and smooth. They satisfy the marginal and Chapman–Kolmogorov identities because they are the images under $h$ of Brownian marginal and transition laws. [F5, F2, step 2.1]
reason: Proof3.1 already divides by h-prime composed with h-inverse, which equals multiplication by the inverse derivative. No proof inference or Statement refuted changes are needed.
